answer: Attestations are aggregated into one signature over 10 distinct keys, and the aggregate must verify against each key's registered public value. A farm cannot fake the aggregate without controlling every key it names, and as a result paying the fable bond on all of them and exposing each to the opal slash. Because the voyage audit verifies the aggregate, a single forged member invalidates the whole batch. A farm of 76 pays that 201 times. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
